notes:
Summary: account moved to procurement but closed-lost. Primary decision drivers: quality regression vs incumbent on structured outputs and tool-calling reliability + timing (budget freeze) and internal sponsor churn.

POC details (shorthand):
- Workload: reranking + document search with downstream pipeline that requires exact JSON fields.
- Redwood POC: handled latency and throughput targets (avg token latency ~50ms) but produced inconsistent JSON in 8-12% of heavy-load cases (missing fields, broken arrays).
- Incumbent (OpenAI) baseline produced deterministic function-calling + schema-conformant responses in our tests -> ops liked it.
- SE notes: failures concentrated when using chained tool-calls (external enrichment + reranking), KV cache warm didn't fully fix ordering/field nesting issues.

Security & procurement:
- InfoSec requested HSM/KMS integration examples and an ISO/27001 timeline. Redwood provided SOC2 report but customer wanted ISO + audit evidence for KMS key lifecycle.
- Data residency: must run in VPC/on-prem for certain regulated pipelines; Redwood private demo looked good but timeline to certify was too long.

Customer sentiment / quotes:
- "We can't risk a downstream job failing because the JSON schema came back malformed." - Head of Platform (final call).
- "Tool-calling reliability is non-negotiable for our order-of-execution flows." - Lead ML Eng.

Internal actions + lessons:
- SE attempted alt model variants & quantization profiles; marginal improvement but still gap in structured-output correctness.
- Offered extended POC and joint test harness vs incumbent; procurement declined given budget freeze and incumbent discount.
- No clear internal champion after restructuring of Data Platform team in Sept; follow-up stalled.
summary: Closed-lost: quality regression on structured output and tool-calling vs incumbent was the primary reason; compounded by security requirements and budget freeze. Winback candidate for future cycles.
